sections.title: Iran War and the Gulf
sections.summary: IRGC claims seven ships hit and threatens US bases; Tehran says indirect talks continue

paragraphs.heading: Seven ships claimed
paragraphs.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy said it simultaneously struck four vessels doing ship-to-ship oil transfers in the northern Persian Gulf and that three more caught fire after hitting mines west of the Strait of Hormuz, Tasnim, TASS and bne IntelliNews reported. The IRGC did not name the ships or give casualty figures, and the claims have not been independently verified. [[TAG:danger:unverified]]

paragraphs.heading: Threat to US bases
paragraphs.body: The IRGC warned it would 'extend confrontation to US bases' in the region if Washington keeps urging ships through what it calls mined waterways, Al Jazeera reported. CBS News reported the US military has quietly reduced its footprint at some Middle East posts because of threats from Iran and the Houthis. [[TAG:warning:base threat]]

paragraphs.heading: Talks or no talks
paragraphs.body: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said indirect negotiations continue over Iran's seven-day ceasefire proposal, with the US seeking new clauses, CBS News reported. Trump denied that negotiations are happening and said the situation would resolve 'fairly soon', according to Al Jazeera. Netanyahu denied that Trump had stopped a planned Israeli attack on Iran, Iran International reported.

sections.sources: Tasnim, TASS, bne IntelliNews, ABC News, Al Jazeera, CBS News, Fox News, Iran International

sections.title: Saudi Arabia Under Fire
sections.summary: Drone debris kills two at Aramco's Shaybah field; US orders diplomats out of Saudi Arabia

paragraphs.heading: Shaybah strike
paragraphs.body: Saudi air defenses intercepted a drone aimed at Aramco's Shaybah field on Wednesday; debris set a contractor's vehicle ablaze outside the perimeter and killed two foreign workers, the Saudi Energy Ministry said, adding that operations were unaffected, Business Recorder and The National reported. The Houthis claimed a wave of attacks including Shaybah, Yanbu and the Riyadh and Abha airports. The Jerusalem Post reported a deadly Houthi attack on Dammam's King Fahd airport. [[TAG:danger:2 killed]]

paragraphs.heading: US drawdown
paragraphs.body: The State Department ordered non-essential staff and families to leave the US Embassy in Riyadh and its consulates, citing Houthi attacks on airports and infrastructure, the AP and Al Jazeera reported. It is the second such order this year; other Gulf missions face temporary staffing changes, Reuters reported via US News. [[TAG:warning:ordered departure]]

sections.title: Ukraine and Russia
sections.summary: Putin agrees in principle to trilateral talks near Nov 10; WSJ says Musk ordered Starlink slowdown

paragraphs.heading: November talks
paragraphs.body: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Putin told envoy Steve Witkoff that Russia is ready in principle to resume trilateral negotiations around November 10, likely in Abu Dhabi, CNN and Liga.net reported. A US official told Axios the proposal for technical-level talks was accepted by Ukraine in Oslo and Russia in St. Petersburg. Ushakov said Ukraine must make 'necessary decisions' and that the Oslo talks offered little of use, CBS News reported. Putin also raised Russia mediating between the US and Iran. [[TAG:info:talks Nov 10]]

paragraphs.heading: Starlink slowdown
paragraphs.body: Elon Musk ordered last week's slowdown of the military-grade Starlink service Ukraine relies on, leaving some Ukrainian drones virtually inoperable, the Wall Street Journal reported, according to CNBC, Bloomberg and the Washington Times. The Journal said Musk and Trump discussed it; Rubio said the administration had no foreknowledge and did not request it. [[TAG:warning:contested account]]

paragraphs.heading: Overnight strikes
paragraphs.body: Moscow's mayor said 630 Ukrainian drones were tracked over the Moscow region overnight, and Russia's Defense Ministry said it intercepted 808 across Russia and Crimea, The Moscow Times reported. Russian strikes killed at least seven people across Ukraine and wounded 15 in Kyiv, The Moscow Times and Cyprus Mail reported. [[TAG:danger:7 killed]]

sections.title: Markets and Big Tech Earnings
sections.summary: SpaceX soars, Meta burns cash on AI, Tesla slips; Asia sells off Thursday as Brent tops $110

paragraphs.heading: Wednesday's close
paragraphs.body: The Dow rose 0.69% to 52,856.09, the S&P 500 gained 0.58% to 7,757.17 and the Nasdaq added 1.05% to 26,702.86, CNBC and Yahoo Finance reported, lifted by strong results from SpaceX and Capital One. One market update reported a flat Nasdaq, conflicting with those figures. [[TAG:success:S&P +0.6%]]

paragraphs.heading: SpaceX and Meta
paragraphs.body: SpaceX shares jumped about 10% intraday after revenue rose 161% to $14.6 billion and Musk said SpaceX and Tesla had formed special committees to discuss a possible merger, CNBC and ABC News reported. Meta's revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, but a $9.89 billion legal charge cut earnings per share to $3.83 and capex of $34.9 billion pushed free cash flow negative, Fortune reported; shares rose after hours, with reported gains ranging from 2.5% to 5%.

paragraphs.heading: Tesla
paragraphs.body: Tesla earned an adjusted $0.48 a share versus about $0.45 expected on revenue of roughly $28 billion, but operating income fell 56% as AI and robotics spending rose, Investing.com and Chartmill reported. Shares slipped after hours as management cut capex guidance to about $20 billion and slowed its Optimus robot timeline; sources disagree on the size of the move.

paragraphs.heading: Asia and oil
paragraphs.body: Asian markets fell Thursday: one wrap had the Nikkei down about 2.2%, the Kospi about 3.8% and the Hang Seng about 3%, NordFX reported, with earlier readings smaller, according to India TV. Brent rose to about $110.5–$111, HDFC Sky reported, after the Shaybah attack. Saxo said Tesla's capex guidance overshadowed Meta's AI plans. [[TAG:danger:Kospi -3.8%]]

sections.title: US Politics
sections.summary: CNN poll: Trump approval hits new low, Democrats +10; GOP Senate nominees edge away from Trump

paragraphs.heading: New low
paragraphs.body: A CNN/SSRS poll found Trump's approval at a new low and Democrats with a 10-point generic-ballot edge as the midterms enter the final stretch, CNN reported. CNN also reported 19% of registered voters name corruption as their top issue amid a stream of allegations around the administration. [[TAG:danger:record low]]

paragraphs.heading: On the trail
paragraphs.body: Trump rallied in Clemson, South Carolina, where he said Democratic Senate candidate Annie Andrews should lose her medical license, Fox News reported. In Senate debates in Michigan and Kansas, Republican nominees Mike Rogers and Roger Marshall made careful breaks with Trump, CNN reported.

paragraphs.heading: Voter-roll lawsuit
paragraphs.body: Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer and House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries sued the administration over voter rolls ahead of the election, Fox News reported.

sections.title: Israel and Lebanon
sections.summary: Eisenkot leads most polls after Gantz quits race; Tampa military talks end without breakthrough

paragraphs.heading: Polls after Gantz
paragraphs.body: After Benny Gantz's Blue and White withdrew, a Walla poll had Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar at 23 seats and Likud at 19, The Jerusalem Post reported, and Haaretz said new polls show Eisenkot's bloc ahead but short of a 61-seat majority. One rolling average still put Likud first, so pollsters disagree. Two parties hover near the 3.25% threshold. Israel votes October 27. [[TAG:info:no majority]]

paragraphs.heading: Tampa stalemate
paragraphs.body: US-mediated military talks between Israel and Lebanon in Tampa made no breakthrough, MTV Lebanon reported. Israel pressed for a joint operations room with Lebanon's army to verify two pilot withdrawal zones; Beirut rejected giving Israel any role over its army's movements. No withdrawal timetable or cessation of hostilities was announced.

sections.title: Europe
sections.summary: French unions call Nov 5 mobilisation; Storm Adam kills five in Spain; Romania gets new cabinet

paragraphs.heading: France
paragraphs.body: French unions left talks with the government disappointed and called a large mobilisation for November 5, and France plans a major police surge ahead of more weekend protests, The Rio Times and Euronews reported. [[TAG:warning:more protests]]

paragraphs.heading: Around the continent
paragraphs.body: Ursula von der Leyen said EU sanctions on Russia stay until the war ends, and the Commission ruled out resuming Russian gas purchases. Storm Adam killed at least five people in eastern Spain, Euronews reported. Romania's new government under Prime Minister Luca Niculescu took office, Poland's Sejm voted to ease some abortion restrictions, and thousands marched in Athens for education funding. Doctors said Pope Leo needs no further treatment after his cancer surgery.

sections.title: Global Roundup
sections.summary: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case in a decade; drone strike on Abyei market; China warns on AI

paragraphs.heading: Ebola reaches Nigeria
paragraphs.body: Nigeria confirmed a Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja in a woman who traveled from eastern Congo via Uganda, and is tracing 44 contacts, mostly health workers, AP and CNBC Africa reported. Uganda says transit does not mean she was infected there. Africa CDC called an emergency meeting of health ministers, OkayAfrica reported. [[TAG:danger:new country]]

paragraphs.heading: Abyei and the Sahel
paragraphs.body: A drone strike on a market in Abyei, near the Sudan-South Sudan border, killed 150 people, Al Jazeera reported; The Rio Times cited a lower toll of 73. Burkina Faso's parliament voted unanimously to restore the death penalty, and Morocco appointed Fatima Zahra El Mansouri its first female prime minister, OkayAfrica reported.

paragraphs.heading: China
paragraphs.body: Former central bank governor Zhou Xiaochuan warned that failed AI investments could cause financial turbulence in China, and China said it allowed a Philippine resupply mission to a warship on a disputed South China Sea shoal, The Wire China and the South China Morning Post reported.
